PICC placement
Peripherally placed PICC line. The arm was prepped and draped in sterile fashion. Lidocaine 1% was used for local anesthetic. Under fluoroscopic and ultrasound guidance, the vein was patent and accessed with a micropuncture needle. A guide wire was then advanced into the vein. After confirmation of the catheter position, the catheter was sutured in place at the skin entry site.

[No focal consolidation / Patchy opacity at the [Right/Left] base may represent atelectasis or contusion].

PLEURAL SPACES:
[No pleural effusion / There is a [small/moderate] [Right/Left] pleural effusion, possibly hemothorax in the setting of trauma]. [No pneumothorax / Pneumothorax as described above].

HEART & MEDIASTINUM: The heart size is [normal]. The mediastinal contours are [normal/widened — recommend CT angiography to exclude aortic injury if high-mechanism trauma]. The trachea is midline.

[Fracture alignment is [maintained/displaced with (Number) mm displacement]]. [Flail segment is [present involving ribs (Number) through (Number) / not identified]]. [Sternal fracture is [present/absent]]. [Clavicle fracture is [present/absent]]. [Scapular fracture is [present/absent]]. [No additional fractures identified]. [Subcutaneous emphysema is [present in the (Right/Left) chest wall / absent]]. [Chest wall soft tissue swelling is noted at the fracture site].
SUPPORT DEVICES: [None / Chest tube on the [Right/Left] with tip at (location)].

IMPRESSION: [Acute/Healing] fractures of the [Right/Left] [Number]th through [Number]th ribs [with/without displacement]. [Associated [small pneumothorax / hemothorax / pulmonary contusion / subcutaneous emphysema]]. [No flail chest / Flail segment involving (location)]. [Recommend CT chest for further evaluation if clinically indicated, particularly to assess for occult pneumothorax or solid organ injury].
